questions.stem_latex:
Tom invented a dice game to play on his own. He throws a pair of six-sided dice repeatedly until the difference between the dice is 2 or 3.

If the difference is 2, Tom wins and the game ends.

If the difference is 3, Tom loses and the game ends.

If the difference is any other number, he continues to throw until the difference is a 2 or 3.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.label: d

solutions.latex: Velocity positive means $x$ is increasing; acceleration negative means the graph is concave down. Answer A.
For $x \ge 1$, $f(x) = x+2 \ge 3$, and $f(x) = 1$ for $x < 1$, so the range is $\{1\} \cup [3, \infty)$, not $f(x) \ge 1$. Statement (D) is incorrect. Answer D.

$u = \ln x,\ u' = \dfrac{1}{x},\ v = x^3,\ v' = 3x^2$

$$y' = \dfrac{vu' - uv'}{v^2} = \dfrac{x^2 - 3x^2\ln x}{x^6} = \dfrac{1 - 3\ln x}{x^4}$$

$1 - 3\ln x = 0 \Rightarrow \ln x = \dfrac{1}{3} \Rightarrow x = e^{\frac{1}{3}}$.

$$y = \dfrac{\ln e^{1/3}}{(e^{1/3})^3} = \dfrac{1/3}{e} = \dfrac{1}{3e}$$

The stationary point is a maximum turning point at $\left(e^{\frac{1}{3}}, \dfrac{1}{3e}\right)$. Answer D.

solutions.latex:
In a right triangle with hypotenuse 7 and adjacent side 3, the opposite side is $x$ where $x^2 + 3^2 = 7^2$, so $x^2 = 49 - 9 = 40$ and $x = \sqrt{40}$. Then $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{40}}{7}$.

$\cos\theta < 0$ but $\tan\theta > 0$, so $\theta$ is in Quadrant 3, where sine is negative.

$$\sin\theta = -\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{7}$$

Arithmetic series with $a = 11$, $d = 2$.

$$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\left(2a + (n-1)d\right)$$

$$375 = \dfrac{n}{2}\left(22 + (n-1)2\right)$$

$$750 = n(20 + 2n) = 20n + 2n^2$$

$2n^2 + 20n - 750 = 0$, so $n^2 + 10n - 375 = 0$.

$(n - 15)(n + 25) = 0$, so $n = 15$ or $n = -25$. Since $n > 0$, $n = 15$.

Fifteen terms are needed to give a sum of 375.

Let $\angle ACB = \theta$.

$$\dfrac{9}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{BC}{\sin 50^\circ} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{9\sin 50^\circ}{BC} = 0.7428 \Rightarrow \theta \approx 48^\circ$$

Ambiguous case check: $180^\circ - 48^\circ = 132^\circ$ and $132^\circ + 50^\circ > 180^\circ$, so $\theta$ is acute.

Bearing $= 360^\circ - 48^\circ = 312^\circ$ T.

Alternatively let $\angle ABC = \alpha$: $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{12\sin 50^\circ}{BC} = 0.9903$, so $\alpha = 82^\circ$, and bearing $= 82^\circ + 50^\circ + 180^\circ = 312^\circ$ T.

$$4 = 5\log_a x - 3\log_a x = 2\log_a x$$

$2 = \log_a x$, so $x = a^2$.

$y' = 8x - 6x^2 = 2x(4 - 3x)$, $y'' = 8 - 12x$.

$y' = 0$: $x = 0$ or $x = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

When $x = 0$: $y'' = 8 > 0$ (concave up), so $(0, 0)$ is a minimum turning point.

When $x = \dfrac{4}{3}$: $y'' = 8 - 12 \times \dfrac{4}{3} = -8 < 0$ (concave down), so there is a maximum turning point at $x = \dfrac{4}{3}$, $y = 4\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^3 = \dfrac{64}{27}$.

$y'' = 8 - 12x = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 0 & \tfrac{2}{3} & \tfrac{4}{3} \\ \hline y'' & 8 & 0 & -8 \\ \text{concavity} & \text{up} & & \text{down} \end{array}$$

The concavity changes at $x = \dfrac{2}{3}$, so there is an inflection point there; $y = \dfrac{32}{27}$.

solutions.latex: $V = \pi r^2 h$, so $160\pi = \pi r^2 h$ and $h = \dfrac{160}{r^2}$.

Cost of top and bottom $= 2 \times \pi r^2 \times 10 = 20\pi r^2$.

Area of curved surface $= 2\pi r h = 2\pi r \times \dfrac{160}{r^2} = \dfrac{320\pi}{r}$; cost $= \dfrac{320\pi}{r} \times 8 = \dfrac{2560\pi}{r}$.

Total $C = 20\pi r^2 + 2560\pi r^{-1}$.

$\dfrac{dC}{dr} = 40\pi r - 2560\pi r^{-2}$, $C'' = 40\pi + \dfrac{5120\pi}{r^3}$.

$\dfrac{dC}{dr} = 0$: $\dfrac{2560\pi}{r^2} = 40\pi r \Rightarrow r^3 = 64 \Rightarrow r = 4$.

When $r = 4$, $C'' = 40\pi + \dfrac{5120\pi}{64} > 0$, so this is a minimum.
